analysis: The batch contains only documentation edits: docs/developer/build.md, navigation.md and test.md. They remove references to the retained console-ui snapshot, its make targets (ui-install, ui-build, ui-lint, ui-test), its CI lane and its pre-commit hook, and point to the platform repository for the web console. No provider code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, cache storage or fan helper behavior changes, so none of TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012 or T-041 (prefix cache) semantics are touched. The security-relevant statements are unchanged: the build.md identity table, SDK 27 release builds, cache separation, App Attest release qualification and the "no backend code uploaded here" rule. Removing the console CI lane and hook reduces in-repo attack surface; console security tests now live in the platform repository, outside this review's scope. One minor documentation inconsistency: build.md line 6-8 still says the existing console snapshot and its build/lint/test/hosting configuration remain here, and line 1 still says 'Retained Console', contradicting navigation.md lines 13-14 and test.md. Navigation.md line 49 also still says 'retained-console docs stay local'. These are stale docs, not a security regression. The 'Verify' and CI routing table edits do not weaken provider release gates. I could not see the actual deletions of console-ui/, workflows or Makefile targets, because those files are not in this batch. I cannot confirm that no remaining provider test or fixture still depends on the shared protocol JSON fixtures, which the docs say must stay in agreement with the provider resource copies. Integration should check that those fixtures and the provider-side tests stay intact.
